before_step.derivation: From accepted step 1, the state space is Z4 x Z3 (12 states) and transitions are deterministic: F0(s,t)=((s+t) mod 4,(t+1) mod 3), F1(s,t)=((2s+t+1) mod 4,(s+t) mod 3), with both coordinates computed from the pre-input state. Define, for each k in {0,...,12}, each j in {0,...,k}, and each state (s,t) in Z4 x Z3, N_{k,j}(s,t) = number of length-k input prefixes whose bits contain exactly j ones and which drive the machine from the initial state (1,0) to state (s,t). Base case: the empty prefix has length 0, contains zero ones, and leaves the machine at (1,0), so N_{0,0}(1,0)=1, and N_{0,j}(s,t)=0 for every other (j,s,t). Recurrence: a length-(k+1) prefix with j ones is formed by appending one bit to a length-k prefix. If the appended bit is 0, the prefix has the same number j of ones and the next state is F0 of the old state; if the appended bit is 1, the prefix has j ones contributed from the old j-1 ones plus this bit, and the next state is F1 of the old state. Because F0 and F1 are functions (step 1), each length-k prefix with a given j extends to exactly one length-(k+1) prefix with that j for input 0 and exactly one for input 1, and distinct prefixes give distinct extensions, so the counts add without multiplicity error: N_{k+1,j}(s,t) = [F0^{-1}(s,t) contributions] + [F1^{-1}(s,t) contributions], i.e. N_{k+1,j}(s,t) = sum over states (u,v) with F0(u,v)=(s,t) of N_{k,j}(u,v) + sum over states (u,v) with F1(u,v)=(s,t) of N_{k,j-1}(u,v). This is a finite recurrence over k=0..12 and j=0..7, requiring only step 1's transition functions; no probabilities enter.
before_step.result: N_{0,0}(1,0)=1 and all other N_{0,j}(s,t)=0; for k+1>=1, N_{k+1,j}(s,t)=sum_{F0(u,v)=(s,t)}N_{k,j}(u,v)+sum_{F1(u,v)=(s,t)}N_{k,j-1}(u,v) over Z4 x Z3, with j ranging 0..k+1.

For the recurrence, take a length-(k+1) prefix with j ones ending at (s,t). Its last bit is either 0 or 1, a disjoint partition. If the last bit is 0, deleting it gives a length-k prefix with j ones ending at some (u,v) such that F0(u,v)=(s,t). Conversely, each such length-k prefix appends 0 to give a length-(k+1) prefix with j ones ending at (s,t), and distinct prefixes give distinct extensions. Thus the last-bit-0 contribution is the sum of N_{k,j}(u,v) over all (u,v) with F0(u,v)=(s,t). If the last bit is 1, deleting it gives a length-k prefix with j-1 ones ending at some (u,v) such that F1(u,v)=(s,t), and conversely appending 1 gives the required prefix. Thus the last-bit-1 contribution is the sum of N_{k,j-1}(u,v) over all (u,v) with F1(u,v)=(s,t). Adding the disjoint cases gives the recurrence, with out-of-range terms such as j-1<0 or j>k treated as zero. No probabilities are needed for this counting step.
